hypotheses.justification: The proof uses invertibility at only one point: `locIsoOnBase_dual`, which calls `IsInvertible.pullback_dual_monoidalV2` along the open immersion `(f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι` to get `j^*(dual 𝓛) ≅ dual (j^* 𝓛)`. Steps h1, h2 and h3 and `LocIsoOnBase.tensor` do not need invertibility. `LocIsoOnBase g M M'` (Def_AlgebraicGeometry_PolarisationRosati) only asks that, around each point of the base, the pullbacks of M and M' along the open immersion `(g ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι` be isomorphic. `Scheme.Modules.dual L` is defined as `(ihom L).obj (𝟙_ _)`. Here `ihom` is the internal Hom of the sheafified monoidal structure on X.Modules (`Monoidal.Reflective.monoidalClosed`), so up to isomorphism it is the sheaf Hom 𝓗om(L, 𝒪_X). Pulling back along an open immersion j : V ↪ X is restriction to V, and restriction commutes with sheaf Hom for every sheaf of modules (Stacks 01CM: 𝓗om(F,G)|_V = 𝓗om(F|_V, G|_V)). So `j^*(dual M) ≅ dual (j^* M)` holds for every 𝓛, invertible or not. Then `locIsoOnBase_dual` holds without the invertibility hypotheses: compose this iso with `dualIso e` as in the existing proof. The rest of the proof is unchanged. I did not find a Mathlib lemma stating this compatibility for open immersions, so that step would need a new proof. Deleting h𝓛 alone leaves a true statement, and so does deleting h𝓛' alone or both together.

Same argument as for h𝓛, applied to 𝓛'. The only use is `pullback_dual_monoidalV2 (f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι h𝓛'` inside `locIsoOnBase_dual`. It provides the iso `j^*(dual 𝓛') ≅ dual (j^* 𝓛')` for the open immersion j = `(f ⁻¹ᵁ U).ι`. That iso holds for any 𝒪_A-module, because the internal Hom on X.Modules is (up to iso) sheaf 𝓗om, and sheaf 𝓗om commutes with restriction to an open subset (Stacks 01CM). So the conclusion still holds without h𝓛', and the rest of the proof (pullback_of_comp_eq, tensor) does not use it.
